name: Mount Birdwood
blurb: Mount Birdwood is the highest peak of the Spray Mountains, on the east edge of Banff National Park above the Birdwood Lakes. Its ridges give long rock climbs well beyond the reach of ordinary scrambles.

name: Mount Cline
blurb: Mount Cline is the highest peak in Clearwater County, a remote summit of the Cline Range north of Saskatchewan Crossing along the David Thompson Highway. It is a big alpine day or an overnight with a bivy at the tarns.

name: Mount Lefroy
blurb: Mount Lefroy is a glaciated summit of the Bow Range on the Alberta-British Columbia line, rising directly above Abbot Pass between Lake Louise and Lake O'Hara. Its usual route climbs snow slopes on the west side from the pass.

name: Mount Northover
blurb: Mount Northover is a 3,048 m summit on the Continental Divide on the Alberta and British Columbia border, standing at the head of the Three Isle, Aster and Joffre creek valleys in the Kananaskis backcountry. It is a serious scrambler's peak, usually reached from camps at Aster or Three Isle lakes.

name: Mount Smuts
blurb: Mount Smuts is a limestone peak in the Spray Mountains on the boundary of Peter Lougheed Provincial Park and Banff National Park. It is known as one of the most serious scrambles in the Kananaskis area, with very few parties summiting each year.

name: South Pioneer Peak
blurb: South Pioneer Peak is the trail-accessible southern summit of Pioneer Peak, the Chugach landmark standing over the Knik River valley south of Palmer. A relentless ridge trail climbs from near sea level to a saddle, and a rough scramble leads to the top.

name: Brunswick Mountain
blurb: Brunswick Mountain tops every other summit in the North Shore Mountains, standing above Lions Bay on Howe Sound. It is a strenuous day from the village and is also reached from the Howe Sound Crest Trail.

name: Mount Begbie
blurb: Mount Begbie is the landmark peak of the Gold Range in the Monashee Mountains, rising above Revelstoke on the Columbia River. A steep forest trail leads to a small glacier below its north ridge.

name: Mount Vaux
blurb: Mount Vaux is the northernmost big peak of the Ottertail Range in Yoho National Park, rising above the Trans-Canada Highway and the Hanbury Glacier. It was first climbed in 1901 and is still lightly visited.

name: Ossa Mountain
blurb: Ossa Mountain is a 2,261 m summit in the Tantalus Range northwest of Squamish, with views across the Sunshine Coast ranges and Mount Tantalus. It is the more reachable of the Tantalus peaks, with a scramble as its easiest route.

name: Mount Adams
blurb: Washington's second-highest peak and the largest-volume stratovolcano in the Cascade Range, Mount Adams (Klickitat/Pahto) rises within the Mount Adams Wilderness of the Gifford Pinchot National Forest, its summit straddling the Yakima/Skamania county line and the western edge of the Yakama Nation Reservation. A dozen named glaciers — including the Adams, Klickitat, Lyman and White Salmon — radiate from its broad summit ice cap, feeding everything from the mellow, glissade-friendly South Climb (one of the most-climbed non-technical volcano routes in the state) to serious north- and east-side alpine ice like the Adams Glacier icefall and the rarely-repeated Wilson and Rusk headwalls.

name: Lone Eagle Peak
approach: Follow the valley trail to the lake beneath the peak, a good place to camp. The usual route to the spire circles east under it, runs south, then turns up the east flank.

name: Thompson Peak
blurb: Thompson Peak is the highest summit in Idaho's Sawtooth Range, a granite high point rising above the Redfish Lake area near Stanley in the Sawtooth Wilderness. Its standard route is a long but non-technical day, with trail, off-trail travel past a high alpine lake and only a short Class 3 finish.

name: Sacagawea Peak
blurb: Sacagawea Peak is the highest summit in the Bridger Range, rising above Fairy Lake north of Bozeman. A short, steep trail reaches its summit from the east, while its rocky east face and ribs offer easy fifth-class scrambling and snow chutes that hold into early summer.

name: Diamond Peak
blurb: Diamond Peak is a glacier-carved volcano, less than 100,000 years old, that stands at the center of the Diamond Peak Wilderness south of Willamette Pass, straddling the Cascade crest between Lane and Klamath counties. Its long ridges rise above a lake-dotted forest traversed by the Pacific Crest Trail, and its summit, reached by a non-technical scramble with an exposed final ridge, looks out over the central Oregon Cascades.

name: Three Fingered Jack
approach: Follow the PCT north until it contours around the southern shoulder of the peak, then take the obvious climbers' trail toward the saddle on the south ridge, within about half a mile.

name: Three Sisters Traverses
blurb: Multi-peak link-ups across the Three Sisters. They cross several summits, so they are filed here rather than under any one peak.

name: Wallowa Mountains Traverses
blurb: Ridge traverses and multi-peak scrambles in the Wallowa Mountains. They cross several summits, so they are filed here rather than under any one peak.

name: Mount Rainier
blurb: Mount Rainier is a massive active stratovolcano in Washington's Cascade Range and the highest peak in the state, carrying more glacial ice than any other mountain in the contiguous United States. It draws climbers to routes ranging from the heavily-traveled Disappointment Cleaver to serious, objectively hazardous alpine lines like Liberty Ridge and the Willis Wall.
